newsitem.title: FRANCE: CDR confirms seeks buyer for Artemis stake.
newsitem.headline: CDR confirms seeks buyer for Artemis stake.

text.p: The CDR, the state agency selling assets that belonged to bank Credit Lyonnais, said on Friday it had asked Goldman Sachs to seek a buyer for its 25 percent stake in Artemis, the holding company of French retail baron Francois Pinault.

The Consortium de Realisation (CDR) said in a statement that it "confirms that it has retained international investment bank Goldman Sachs to help in the search for financial or strategic investors which might be interested in taking stakes that it holds in Artemis."
The CDR made no further comment.

The newspaper Le Monde reported earlier that Goldman Sachs was expected to launch a tender for offers soon. It said CDR retained Goldman Sachs in the autumn of 1996 to assess the value of the stake. Artemis' assets include 40 percent of retailer Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, U.S. junk bonds, and the Chateau Latour Bordeaux wines.
Financiere Pinault owns 75 percent of Artemis.
Le Monde said Goldman Sachs faced a challenge in finding a buyer content to be minority shareholders in an unlisted company. "Who would take the risk if not Francois Pinault himself?" it said.
